Why use Spring @Async instead of a blocking call in the validation microservice?
fields.Back: It frees up request-handling threads while waiting on I/O, so more validation requests can be in flight concurrently — improving throughput and latency under load.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Tell me about a time you made a system more resilient to upstream failures."
fields.Back:
S: The Business Experience Platform's validation microservice depended on upstream services that could be slow or fail.
T: Reduce load on and exposure to those upstream dependencies.
A: Added Resilience4j circuit breakers to fail fast on unhealthy upstreams, plus Caffeine in-memory caching to avoid redundant calls.
R: Cut upstream calls by ~25%.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Tell me about optimizing a high-throughput backend service."
fields.Back:
S: The validation microservice on the Business Experience Platform needed to handle input validation for a high volume of business submissions.
T: Reduce request latency without blocking server threads.
A: Rebuilt the validation path using Spring @Async for non-blocking I/O.
R: Achieved 40% lower latency.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Describe a backend system you built that handled real scale."
fields.Back:
S: The Government of Ontario needed eForm back-end architecture for the Business Experience Platform.
T: Design and build it to handle high daily volume across many businesses.
A: Built the back-end in Java + Spring Boot, plus an @Async validation microservice and Resilience4j/Caffeine for resilience and efficiency.
R: The platform handled 10GB+/day for 400,000+ businesses, with 40% lower validation latency and ~25% fewer upstream calls.

fields.Text: Michele built the eForm back-end for the Business Experience Platform in {{c1::Java + Spring Boot}}, handling {{c2::10GB+/day}} for {{c3::400,000+}} businesses.
Michele added {{c1::Resilience4j}} circuit breakers plus {{c2::Caffeine}} caching, cutting upstream calls by {{c3::~25%}}.

fields.Back: A resilience pattern that stops calling a failing or slow upstream service once a failure threshold is hit, failing fast locally instead of letting the failure cascade.
A high-performance in-memory Java caching library, used here to serve repeated lookups locally and reduce redundant upstream calls.
